questions: Does the score reproduce about 70.83 on the development tracks, confirming the base is stable across seeds?
Are line losses still one per run on the s-bend and slalom, at the same bend and step as before?
Does any controller path reduce the s-bend or slalom line loss without raising steering_oscillation above about 0.15, so the final unseen-track run benefits?

intent: Hold the iteration 6 geometry as the final base, unchanged from the design that scored 70.83 twice (iterations 6 and 10). No untested lever is added, since this is the final iteration and no later race could verify it. Expect a score near 70.8 on development tracks, with one line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom and progress near the earlier values. The Integrator's controller is the only remaining variable on the final unseen track.
learning: Across iterations 6 to 10, the iteration 6 geometry is the only one that has scored 70.83 twice. Mass 0.4 kg is at its floor and is the one geometry change that raised the score in isolation. Span, footprint, track width, forward offset and body length each lowered the score or left line losses unchanged. Wheel_radius 0.035 m remains the only untested single lever, and it was left untested because no later iteration could act on its result. The final score therefore depends on the controller and on how this base transfers to unseen tracks.
rationale:
The iteration 10 race has returned. It reproduces the iteration 6 design exactly: score 70.8269, with one line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom and identical per-track metrics. That confirms the iteration 6 geometry as a stable base, and the score difference in iteration 9 (69.05) came from the 0.14 m track.

The Integrator's conditional branch applies here: the score is near 70.8 with line losses still at 1.0 per run, so the base is confirmed and wheel_radius 0.035 m is the one untested single lever. I considered testing it, but this is the final iteration. Whatever I submit here is the design raced on the unseen final track, and no later iteration exists in which to use what a dev race reveals. Wheel_radius 0.035 m raises speed and turn rate together. Turn rate was the factor that lowered the score when slowed (0.14 m track), and faster turning on the 0.10 m track (iteration 1, confounded) also scored lower. So an untested change would stake the final score on an unverified gain.

I therefore hold the iteration 6 geometry unchanged: mass 0.4 kg, body 0.16 m by 0.12 m, five 12 mm sensors at x = +0.03, +0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03 and y = 0.05 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m. This is the best-evidenced design (70.83 on two independent races). I expect a score near 70.8 on the development tracks, and the final unseen race is the one that depends on how well this base transfers.
